title: Counter Blitz — Upgrade Options
summary: Tidus moves a counter between your creatures each combat, and when creatures with counters deal combat damage to a player you draw a card and proliferate (once a turn). The stock list is already well balanced, so no shared package is needed. Each direction spends all 10 swaps on a sharper plan, cutting the same weak, random or off-plan cards. Budget: up to €20 per deck in total (Cardmarket prices).

notes: Curve is low and healthy (avg MV about 3.0), with only three cards at 6+.
Interaction is fine: ~10 spot removal, 3 board wipes, plus a counterspell.
Protection is solid (5 pieces) and ramp is on target (~10 with 37 lands).
Weak spots: a few random or defensive cards (Summon: Magus Sisters, Lulu, Gatta and Luzzu, Promise of Loyalty), and too few cheap evasive creatures to set off Tidus's Cheer every turn.
Bracket: Farewell is a Game Changer, so the stock deck is bracket 3. Swap it for a non-Game Changer wipe if your table plays bracket 2.

directions.name: Cheer Every Turn
directions.pitch: Make Tidus's Cheer fire every turn: cheap evasive creatures, counters at the start of each combat, and unblockability for anything with a counter. Tekuthal doubles each Cheer's proliferate, and Kutzil stops opponents from responding while you attack.
directions.plays_like: Fast, evasive pressure; draws every turn

swaps.why: 2 mana: a +1/+1 counter on a creature at the start of every combat, so Tidus always has counters to move. Generous Patron only draws when you put counters on creatures you don't control; with Lulu gone, nothing in the deck does that.
Unblockable 2-drop that grows or draws on hit; with a counter it sets off Cheer reliably. Magus Sisters picks its modes at random.
A flyer that draws a card each time a creature with a counter hits a player. A second Cheer on a 3-drop. Sin costs 7.
2-mana flyer that proliferates on hit. Promise of Loyalty makes you sacrifice your own creatures too.
+1 extra counter on every placement (including Tidus's moves) on a 2-mana creature. The same job as Ozolith for €0.26. Yuna's Decision is a clunky 4-mana sorcery.
A 3/5 flyer that doubles every proliferate: Tidus's Cheer, Thrummingbird and Inexorable Tide all proliferate twice. Lulu is defensive; this deck wants to attack.

Every creature you control with a +1/+1 counter can't be blocked, so Cheer triggers every combat. Chasm Skulker is slow; Shelinda stays because she gives a counter to each small evasive creature that enters.
Another +1 to every +1/+1 counter placement, and it taps for mana equal to its power. Resourceful Defense only moves counters around.
2-mana instant: +1/+1 counter and protection from a colour. Saves a creature and pushes damage through. Forgotten Ancient is slow.

Draws a card whenever creatures pumped by counters hit a player, and opponents can't cast spells during your turn, so no removal or tricks while your small evasive creatures attack. Altered Ego is a 4+ mana copy effect with no evasion.
Land swap. Untapped green or blue on its own. Overflowing Basin can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Untapped white or blue on its own. Skycloud Expanse can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. {4},{T}: proliferate, doubled by Tekuthal. Replaces another colourless land that only works with five lands out.

how_to_play.summary: Get one evasive creature with a counter through every turn: Cheer draws a card and proliferates, and the pressure snowballs.

sections.title: How Tidus works
points: Beginning of combat: move a counter from one of your creatures onto another.
Cheer (once per turn): when your creatures with counters deal combat damage to a player, draw a card and proliferate.

sections.title: Turns 1–3: counters plus evasion
points: Counter sources: Luminarch Aspirant, Shelinda, Conclave Mentor or Kami of Whispered Hopes (+1 on every placement), Hardened Scales.
Evasive creatures: Thrummingbird, Silent Hallcreeper (unblockable), Lord Jyscal Guado, Ray Fillet.

sections.title: Each combat, in this order
points: Resolve the counter-placing triggers first (Luminarch, Fight Rigging, Maester Seymour).
Then use Tidus to move a counter onto your best evasive creature. Conclave Mentor, Kami and Hardened Scales boost moved counters too, so one move can be 2–3 counters.
Attack with everything that can't be blocked.

sections.title: Turns 4+: engines
points: Herald of Secret Streams: every creature with a +1/+1 counter is unblockable. This is your most important card.
Kutzil: opponents can't cast spells during your turn, and you draw when pumped creatures connect.
Tekuthal doubles every proliferate (Cheer, Thrummingbird, Grateful Apparition, Karn's Bastion, Inexorable Tide, Tromell).
Ray Fillet, Bred for the Hunt and Blitzball Stadium draw on hits; Chocobo Knights gives your creatures with counters double strike when you attack.

sections.title: Wipes and tips
points: Damning Verdict destroys only creatures without counters, so it's usually one-sided. Farewell is your reset when behind (and the deck's only Game Changer).
When you proliferate you choose what grows: skip opponents, grow your shield counters from Protection Magic.
Hold up protection (Feat of Resistance, Protection Magic, Inspiring Call, Gatta and Luzzu with flash). Two or three evasive threats plus Herald is enough; don't overextend into a wipe.
Mulligan hands without a 2-drop counter source or an evasive creature.

directions.name: Proliferate Engine
directions.pitch: Every proliferate adds +1/+1, shield and lore counters together, and draws cards. Tidus's Cheer becomes one engine among many.
directions.plays_like: Value engine; grows everything at once

swaps.why: Draws a card every time you proliferate, and can proliferate twice on entering.
Proliferate on every land drop.
Proliferate on every noncreature spell.
2-drop: proliferate whenever another nontoken creature enters under your control.
Two +1/+1 counters every combat; tap to double every kind of counter on two permanents.
3/3 that puts a shield counter on a creature or proliferates when it enters. Not random.
Evasive 2-drop that proliferates on hit.
Instant: proliferate, then phase out your creatures that have counters. Doubles as protection from a board wipe.
Instant: look at three, take one, proliferate. Cheap selection that also grows your board.
Gives a shield counter on entering, and pumps an attacker by its number of counter kinds.

how_to_play.summary: Proliferate as often as possible: every +1/+1, shield and lore counter grows together, and Ezuri turns each proliferate into a card.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Proliferate sources: Evolution Sage (each land), Flux Channeler (each noncreature spell), Metastatic Evangel (each nontoken creature entering), Thrummingbird (on hit), Tidus's Cheer.
Ezuri draws a card every time you proliferate; Zimone puts counters out each combat and can double counters on two permanents.
Proud Pack-Rhino and Perrie add shield counters, which proliferate keeps growing.

sections.title: Tips
points: Ripples of Potential proliferates and phases out your countered creatures: hold it for an opponent's board wipe.
Experimental Augury is a cheap instant: dig a card and proliferate at the end of an opponent's turn.
Sequence cheap noncreature spells after Flux Channeler is out to proliferate several times per turn.

directions.name: Go Tall Hydras
directions.pitch: Double your counters and attack with a few huge creatures. Tidus moves the counters to the creature that can connect, and Herald of Secret Streams makes them unblockable.
directions.plays_like: A few enormous threats; ends games fast

swaps.why: Doubles the +1/+1 counters on every creature you control each time it attacks. A cheaper and stronger top end than Sin.
Pay X; it doubles its own counters every upkeep and gains trample at 10.
Doubles every kind of counter put on your creatures, including shield counters. Warp lets you cast it for {G} early.
2-drop: +1 extra counter on every placement.
Another +1 extra counter on every placement, and a mana sink that puts counters on legendary creatures (Tidus has lots of legendary support).
Scales with X, adds +1 to counters on your other creatures, and can move its own counters.
A counter doubler on a 4/4 body; its power-up puts three counters on itself.
Trample, and gets a +1/+1 counter whenever any player casts a spell. Doublers make it huge fast.
Add a counter, then double it. Overload it to double the counters on every creature you control.
Creatures with +1/+1 counters can't be blocked, so the huge creatures connect.

how_to_play.summary: Double your counters, then attack with one or two enormous creatures that can't be blocked.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Doublers and boosters: Loading Zone (doubles every kind of counter), Shang-Chi (doubler on a body), Conclave Mentor, Yoshimaru, Benevolent Hydra (+1 each).
Threats: Kalonian Hydra (doubles all your +1/+1 counters when it attacks), Primordial Hydra (doubles itself each upkeep), Managorger Hydra (grows whenever anyone casts a spell).
Herald of Secret Streams makes them unblockable; Fangs of Kalonia overloaded doubles every creature's counters.

sections.title: Tips
points: Use Tidus to move counters onto the creature that can connect, or away from a creature about to be removed.
Spread threats across two creatures so one removal spell doesn't end your game.

recommendation: Cheer Every Turn fixes the deck's one real weakness, which is how reliably Cheer fires. It's also cheap and lowers the curve. Go Tall Hydras hits harder but leans on a few big creatures that are easier to answer. All three stay under €20.
